description: Change of use from C3 dwellinghouse to 8-person Large HMO (Sui Generis). Erection of a two-storey wraparound extension (side and rear). Outbuilding demolition, installation of bin/cycle stores and amenity space.
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of the change of use of the property from a self-contained dwellinghouse to an 8-person House in Multiple Occupation within a sui generis use, would result in the loss of a dwelling capable of family occupation and has failed to demonstrate that this loss would be justified having regard to the Council's adopted housing mix objectives. The proposed HMO would also fail to demonstrate compliance with the Council's adopted policy framework for HMOs, having regard to the intensity of occupation, substandard living conditions for future occupiers, unacceptable harm to neighbouring residential amenity and the failure to demonstrate adequate and deliverable parking provision. The proposal would therefore represent an unacceptable and over-intensive form of HMO accommodation in this location, contrary to Policies DMH 2 and DMH 5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies H9 and H10 of the London Plan (2021), and the objectives of the National Pl

The proposed extensions, by reason of their cumulative bulk and large crown roof design, would result in an unsympathetic, bulky and visually incongruous form of development which would fail to respect the scale, proportions, roof form, and detailed design of the original building. The proposed crown roof would be contrary to Policy DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), which states that large crown roofs on will not be supported, and would appear as an incongruous feature within the established roofscape of the Conservation Area. The proposal would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Conservation Area, resulting in less than substantial harm to its significance which would not be outweighed by the limited public benefits of the proposal. The development would therefore be contrary to Policies DMHB 1, DMHB 4, DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy HC1 of the London P

In the absence of submitted detail or evidence with regard to the level of present on-street parking demand within the locality and whether any spare capacity exists which could satisfactorily accommodate potential parking displacement generated by the proposed level of occupancy, it is considered that the proposal has the potential to lead to undue on-street parking displacement to the detriment of parking capacity and safety on the local public highway, contrary to Local Plan: Part 2 Development Management Plan (2020) - Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 & DMT 6 and Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed development, by reason of its increased number of independent occupiers, would generate materially greater noise, comings and goings, and garden use than the existing C3 dwelling, resulting in unacceptable disturbance to neighbouring residents. The submitted HMO Management Plan does not adequately mitigate these effects. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of its over-intensive layout, lack of communal living room, and the direct relationship between Rooms 2, 3 and 4 and the communal rear garden, would provide a substandard level of accommodation for future occupiers. The rear garden, which would also be accessed from the communal kitchen/dining area, is likely to be used frequently as a principal communal/social space by up to 8 occupiers. This would result in unacceptable noise, disturbance, overlooking and loss of privacy to the occupiers of Rooms 2, 3 and 4. As such, notwithstanding the size of the individual bedrooms, the proposal would fail to provide a high-quality residential environment for future occupiers. The development is therefore contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11 and DMHB 16 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the National Planning Policy Framework.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
